ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the Government of Canada's sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 19; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21), OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated list, and the FINTRAC PEP definition. Verify identity under client identification rules, monitor transaction activity, and conduct enhanced due diligence for any foreign PEP, immediate family member, or close associate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under O. Reg. 62/06, names must be in an English or French form or a transliteration; if bilingual, both forms appear on records; the name must not contain a word or phrase that is likely to mislead the public about the business's actual character; numerals may be included.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a refusal from the Director, submit written reconsideration to Ontario Business Registry / Ministry of Public and Business Service and Delivery attaching the NUANS report, amended proposed name, and legal argument; if reconsideration is unsuccessful, seek judicial review in the Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, within the limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for OBCA compliance: a registered physical street address in Ontario must be maintained; a P.O. Box is not acceptable. A virtual office service that provides suite number, mail handling, and process service acceptance is acceptable for a Software/SaaS business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% risk due to absence of regulated premises; Ontario authorities may visit only to verify registered office existence, but not for premises-based licensing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16 (OBCA), ss. 3-13 (incorporation), s. 23 (share consideration), s. 115 (registered office), ss. 119-126 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CIPPSB), operating the Ontario Business Registry (OBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under the OBCA, as prescribed by O. Reg. 62/13)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required; no escrow account mandated under Ontario law. Shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine adequate (OBCA s. 23(2)). The corporation may commence business immediately upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopt the registered office described in the Articles of Incorporation, and that any change be filed with the Ontario Business Registry under OBCA section 115; RESOLVED, that the subscription for the initial common shares be accepted, and that the shares be allotted and issued to the subscriber for the consideration recorded in the share register under OBCA section 23; RESOLVED, that the following officers be appointed: Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, with authority to manage business, open bank accounts, execute contracts, and sign statutory filings; RESOLVED, that management be authorized to complete all ancillary filings for the Corporation's activation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR) via authorized NUANS service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a mandatory name search request through the OBR or a licensed NUANS report provider. Review the NUANS Preliminary Search Report for conflicting trade names or trademarks. If clear, reserve the proposed name and attach the NUANS report to the Articles of Incorporation. The name reservation may be evidenced in the submitted Articles.
required_dossiers: NUANS Preliminary Search Report (where a proposed corporate name is used)
Ontario jurisdiction statement confirming registered office will be in Ontario
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or is confusingly similar, select an alternative name and resubmit a fresh NUANS search. No material procedural cure fee is charged at the OBR correction stage; the registry will flag the deficiency and allow re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Articles of Incorporation and Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry online portal (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation online. Specify the corporate name, registered office address (must be an Ontario street address), first directors (names, addresses, and consent), share structure (classes, rights, and restrictions), and any restrictions on business. Pay the CAD 300 electronic filing fee. Upon approval, the OBR issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which vests the corporation with legal personality.
required_dossiers: Form 2 - Consent of Director (or incorporated consent in the Articles)
Share structure and class rights description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of deficiency (e.g., name conflict, incomplete director consent, or invalid share class), correct the flagged fields in the OBR portal and re-submit within the prescribed cure period. The Certificate is issued only after full compliance; no penalty is assessed for first-instance corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Return Filing and Corporate Profile Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of the date of incorporation, file the Initial Return under the Ontario Corporations Information Act, confirming the registered office address, directors' names and addresses, and the corporation's principal activity. Maintain the Corporate Profile Report as the authoritative public record and update it whenever director or office information changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is incomplete or rejected, amend and re-file electronically via the OBR. Late filing may attract penalties under the Corporations Information Act; the cure is to file immediately and request administrative relief where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number (BN) through the CRA BRO portal using the Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Return data. Open the corporate income tax account (RC), and, if applicable, GST/HST (RT) and payroll (RP) program accounts. Use the BN for banking identification, tax filings, and vendor onboarding.
required_dossiers: Director identification (SIN or passport for registration)
Registered office address and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is not automatically issued, contact CRA Business Enquiries at 1-800-959-5525. Correct any data mismatches between the OBR records and the BRO application; the CRA will issue the BN once the validation succeeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Minute Book Formation and Organizational Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the corporation acting through the Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory minute book containing the Articles, By-law No. 1, share register, organizational resolutions, and minutes of the First Board Meeting (including adoption of the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution). Issue share certificates to the subscribers. Record the appointment of officers and the authorization of banking signatories, and ensure all records are kept at the registered office for inspection.
required_dossiers: OBCA Form 2 (Consent of Director, if not previously filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ontario registrar, CRA, or a financial institution requires governance records, cure by producing the executed resolutions and corrected corporate records. Any omission in director or officer consent is remedied by a retroactive written resolution signed by all directors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board or sectoral permit is mandated for pure Fleet Route Optimization and Real-Time Telematics SaaS operations under Ontario law; only a municipal business licence (e.g., City of Toronto Municipal Licensing & Standards) is required if an office premises is maintained.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating licence required for software development and cloud-based SaaS; voluntary registrations include PIPEDA privacy compliance (Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada) and CRA GST/HST registration for revenue realization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based SaaS activity is not listed in Schedule 4 of O. Reg. 337/16 (Environmental Activity and Sector Registry); no full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) or EASR registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core activity. For leased office premises, general HVAC wastewater discharge and solid waste handling must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and O. Reg. 588/17 (Ontario Building Code); site-specific air emission limits under O. Reg. 419/05 are not triggered by standard office occupancy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance under O. Reg. 213/07 (Ontario Fire Code) administered by the local fire department; structural load inspection under O. Reg. 332/12 (Ontario Building Code) for the leased office; workplace health and safety compliance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1, enforced by the Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including its Business Registration Online portal at canada.ca/business-registration, GST/HST NETFILE, and My Business Account; provincial corporate registration and Ontario tax matters are administered by ServiceOntario and the Ontario Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity with Canadian nexus first obtains a federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online, or by filing Form RC1 if applying on paper; the BN is the sole federal tax identifier for corporate income tax and GST/HST, with no separate national VAT identification number. If the entity is carrying on business in Ontario under a federal or extra-provincial structure, it must complete the applicable extra-provincial registration through ServiceOntario before filing tax accounts. A non-resident supplier of SaaS or telematics-related digital services whose Canadian taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold must open a CRA GST/HST account through the simplified foreign supplier registration pathway; registration may be required even without a Canadian permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election or pass-through election is available for a Canadian Business Corporation; the entity is categorically subject to federal Part I and Ontario corporate income tax at the entity level. Relevant statutory elections for cross-border structures include the section 85 rollover for transfers of eligible property, the section 216(1) election for net-basis Canadian-source rental income, and allocation rules among associated corporations under section 256. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are governed by Income Tax Act section 18.4 to 18.6 and OECD BEPS Action 2 principles; there is no elective regime or opt-out mechanism, and CRA may also apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST Harmonized Sales Tax (federal Goods and Services Tax harmonized with Ontario Provincial Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; a person ceases to be a small supplier and must register for GST/HST once total worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Non-resident digital suppliers of SaaS and related services must register when Canadian-source taxable digital-service revenues exceed CAD 30,000 on an annual basis; once registered, HST at 13% applies to Canadian taxable supplies unless a zero-rating provision applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, pre-clearance API submission, or digital stamping at the federal or Ontario level. Electronic invoices are legally valid and must contain the supplier's Business Number, invoice date, description of the supply, amount of consideration, and applicable GST/HST rate and tax payable. GST/HST returns are filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE, EDI, or CRA-approved API channels. SaaS billing via Stripe or wire transfer is acceptable provided the statutory invoice particulars and supporting records are preserved for the required six-year retention period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, goods exported from Canada are zero-rated if the exporter maintains contemporaneous proof of exportation and the goods are delivered outside Canada. For logistics-technology SaaS and telematics platform access, a supply made to a non-resident recipient is eligible for zero-rating when the recipient is outside Canada at the time of supply, the supply is not attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment of the recipient, and the supply is not primarily for use in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The exporter must retain commercial, shipping, and payment evidence to substantiate the zero-rated treatment on the GST/HST return and underlying input tax credit claims.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or Canada Border Services Agency electronic export report) or equivalent inward/outward export proof
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the non-resident buyer, terms of sale, and nature of the digital service or goods
Bill of Lading or airway bill (original or certified carrier copy) showing movement of goods outside Canada or, for digital services, server and user-location evidence
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank SWIFT MT103/credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign or Canadian currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating and claw back input tax credits and refunds where the export document bundle is incomplete, internally inconsistent, or fails to demonstrate that the recipient was outside Canada or that the supply was not connected to Canadian property or users. Penalties include a gross-negligence penalty equal to 25% of the misstated amount subject to a CAD 100 minimum, daily compound interest under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act, failure-to-file and false-return penalties, and criminal liability for fraudulent export claims. The normal four-year reassessment period may be extended or made unlimited where false statements or neglect, carelessness, or wilful default are established, allowing retrospective clawback of HST previously zero-rated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank and sole bank-note issuer. Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority; prudential regulation of chartered banks resides with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/CTF supervision with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and sanctions administration with Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act. Payments infrastructure (LVTS and ACSS) is operated by Payments Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully free-floating, with complete current-account and capital-account convertibility. There are no exchange controls, capital-repatriation permits, or profit-remittance licences. Non-resident shareholders may freely receive dividends, interest, royalties, and disposal proceeds, subject only to Part XIII withholding tax (statutorily 25%, reduced under income tax treaties such as the Canada-US Convention) and to standard Income Tax Act compliance, including T1135 foreign-property reporting when foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000 in cost. No import or conversion of foreign currency is mandated at point of entry; CAD/USD multi-currency operating accounts are standard at all Schedule I banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no export-proceeds surrender rule, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory holding or liquidation timeline. Export and services revenue may remain indefinitely in a foreign-currency operating account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. Statutory conversion ratio: 0%; required timeline: none (0 days). For goods exports, an export declaration must be filed via the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for shipments above CAD 2,000; telematics and SaaS services exports require no customs declaration. Arm's-length transfer pricing and T106 information-return obligations apply to non-resident related-party transactions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - legally permissible but ring-fenced. Foreign digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, etc.) may operate in Canada as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses and, where applicable, must also obtain registration under the Retail Payment Activities Act, supervised by the Bank of Canada. They cannot accept deposits or provide CDIC-insured deposit protection in the manner of a chartered bank, and their offshore fund-safeguarding structures are not eligible for the CDIC guarantee. Viable supplementary use: aggregating US and European customer receivables from Stripe Billing, plus low-value cross-border vendor payouts. The primary settlement hub - capital injection, payroll, creditor payments, and FX hedging - should remain at a Schedule I chartered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal or Ontario statute mandates a physical branch interview. FINTRAC permits identity verification through (i) physical presence, (ii) valid electronic credential or digital attestation, or (iii) reliance on a regulated financial institution's credit-file verification. In practice, Canadian chartered banks require at least one director or authorized signatory to complete a live video interview with government-issued ID and entity documents, and will usually require an in-branch visit only where ownership is complex, a non-resident director cohort exists, or digital verification cannot be satisfied. An Ontario-incorporated logistics-technology corporation with a Canadian-resident director, a registered Ontario address, and a clean AML profile can complete onboarding fully remotely; for non-resident shareholders, a notarized power of attorney appointing a Canadian-resident signing officer is a standard supplementary control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or complex beneficial-ownership structure: foreign parent in a tax-haven jurisdiction, nominee shareholding, or discretionary trust above the 25% UBO threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Business Registry excerpt; articles of incorporation; full shareholder register; UBO declaration on the 25% threshold; entity organization chart; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; tax-residency certificates; trust deed where applicable; legal opinion from Ontario counsel; recently audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed persons, or adverse-media hits under SEMA, UN Act, and OSFI guidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-news and sanctions screening reports (SEMA/UN/OFAC reference where relevant); PEP assessment records; proof of economic substance and physical office in Ontario; senior-management attestation; engagement letter with a recognized compliance advisor; ongoing transaction-monitoring commitment letter to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, rapid inbound capital injection from a non-resident related party (share capital or intercompany loan) with insufficient commercial documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or intercompany loan agreement at market-rate interest; board resolutions approving the financing; transfer-pricing documentation (OECD master/local file and Canadian T106 return); valuation report supporting share consideration; deployment plan linking funds to fleet-dispatch SaaS development and booking of sales; bank statements tracing the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue-profile mismatch: cross-border B2B SaaS revenue with no identifiable physical export triggers enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service contracts with logistics and fleet customers; Stripe Billing settlement statements and SDK agreements; recurring-revenue ledger; sales invoices with correct GST/HST treatment for exported services (zero-rated); intellectual-property ownership registry and software escrow; CPA-compiled financial statements and cash-flow forecasts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory registry or corporate record deficiency: lapse in Ontario annual returns, missing directors, or unresolved PPSA security-interest filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Ontario Business Registry profile; certificate or status letter from the Registry; minute-book extracts; signed by-laws and organizing resolutions; PPSA and writ/execution search reports; banking signatory resolution and specimen signature card.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use the receiving bank's SWIFT rail with the corresponding BIC (e.g., RBC ROYCCAT2, TD TDOMCATTTOR, Scotiabank NOSCCATT, BMO BOFMCAM2, CIBC CIBCCATT). Required inbound-wire fields: beneficiary legal name, Canadian deposit account number, five-digit transit code, three-digit institution code, SWIFT/BIC of the beneficiary bank, and the beneficiary bank's country. Include ISO 20022 payment-purpose code 'EQUI' for equity subscription proceeds or 'LOAN' for intercompany loan advances, and annotate the wire narrative with the applicable resolution or agreement reference. Financial institutions must report electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. For CAD credits above CAD 50,000, settlement occurs in real time through Payments Canada LVTS; for USD credits, finality is achieved through the bank's US clearing subsidiary or via CHIPS/Fedwire. Corporate counsel should retain the subscription agreement, intercompany loan agreement, board resolutions, and the bank's approval memorandum to evidence non-revenue capital treatment for Part I tax and GST/HST purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and revenue-routing payments are executed by SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit), with MT202 for bank-to-bank settlements and MT700 for documentary letters of credit (irrevocable, confirmed or unconfirmed) when financing physical fleet or telematics hardware purchases. CAD-denominated payables and payroll clear through Payments Canada ACSS/EFT direct-deposit rails and LVTS for large-value same-day debits. USD wires should be discharged through the bank's US dollar corridor (e.g., TD Bank N.A., RBC Bank (Georgia), BMO Harris) or via Fedwire/CHIPS for same-day USD finality. For SaaS license royalties and subscription fees, use ISO 20022 purpose code 'ROYA' or 'TRAD' and attach supporting agreements to mitigate the bank's FX/AML review. Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on royalties and management fees must be remitted in the same remittance cycle as the underlying wire, with supporting W-8 series forms maintained on file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (outright and window-forwards, tenors up to 24 months) documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Canadian-law-governed Credit Support Annex
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD fixed-for-floating and USD-floating-to-CAD-fixed) used to match intercompany loan and equipment-lease liabilities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for illiquid or restricted counterparty currencies (e.g., RMB, INR, BRL) settled in CAD/USD on the fixing date where local deliverability is prohibited
European-style vanilla FX options (call or put) and zero-premium collar structures protecting USD-denominated SaaS subscription revenue
On-balance-sheet FX swap and tom-next rollover lines for intraday working-capital optimization and month-end FX translation management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Personal Property Security Branch / ServiceOntario, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; e.g., if incorporated on 15 March, file by 14 May each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and officers face regulatory offence exposure; continued non-filing permits the Director to issue a notice of intention to dissolve, followed by administrative dissolution. Restoration requires a formal application, prescribed Ministry fees, court order where applicable, and additional professional costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not compulsory for this private non-distributing corporation; an audit is mandatory if shareholders holding at least 10% of the issued shares demand it, or if the corporation becomes a distributing corporation under securities legislation. If no auditor is appointed, an annual unanimous shareholder resolution waiving the auditor appointment is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is generally acceptable; the private SaaS entity is expected to use the CPA Canada Handbook Part II – Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) unless a change is formally adopted by the board

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually review the register of members and all share transfer instruments to identify every Individual with Significant Control (25% or more of voting shares or de facto control). Update the Significant Control Register with full legal name, residence, date of entry/exit, and nature of control; obtain board approval and retain the confirmation documents for at least seven years.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal plus Ontario headline for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC): 12.2% for qualifying active business income up to the CAD 500,000 small business deduction limit (federal 9% plus Ontario 3.2%); 26.5% for general active business income above the small business deduction limit (federal 15% after the 10% provincial abatement and 13% general rate reduction, plus Ontario 11.5%). Manufacturing and processing income in Ontario is taxed at a reduced Ontario rate of 10%, producing a 25.0% combined rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC small business deduction: federal rate reduced from 28% to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income (Schedule 4, subject to association rules and the business limit). Ontario small business deduction reduces the Ontario rate from 11.5% to 3.2% on the same CAD 500,000 eligible active business income. Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit: 35% refundable ITC for CCPCs on qualified SR&ED expenditures, reduced when the prior-year taxable income or capital thresholds are exceeded. Ontario Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (ODMTC): 40% refundable credit on qualifying Ontario labour expenditures for eligible interactive digital media products, capped at CAD 22,500 per eligible employee per year; relevant for the fleet route optimization and telematics SaaS platform. No preferential provincial tax holiday applies in Ontario; eligible credits are claimed on the T2 return through Schedules 8 and 23.
